entries.what_happened: Three manuscripts in this family bear on the coefficient-free reduced assembly map (target C*_r(G), coefficient algebra C). (1) 'A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum-Connes injectivity' (dated 23 September 2026) constructs a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group Γ, an injective homomorphism i: Z^2 -> Γ, and a class c in H^2(BΓ; Z) with <(Bi)^*c, [T^2]> = 1, such that i_*(β) = 0 in K_0(C*_r Γ), where β is the rank-zero Bott generator of K_0(C*_r Z^2). Hence h = (Bi)_*[D_{T^2}] in K_0(BΓ) has infinite order, while its reduced assembly image is zero: a nonzero degree-zero kernel element of the reduced assembly map. (2) 'An irrational-trace counterexample to reduced Baum-Connes' (23 September 2026) constructs a finitely generated discrete group Γ_sur = V ⋊ Γ, with V a finite-field module, and a projection b_0 in C*_r(Γ_sur) whose canonical trace is the series sum over i of p^(-k_i), which the manuscript shows is irrational. Every class in the image of degree-zero assembly has rational trace (Lück's trace theorem, as recalled in the text), so [b_0] in K_0(C*_r Γ_sur) lies outside the image: a failure of surjectivity in degree zero. The manuscript states this refutes the coefficient-free reduced conjecture for countable discrete groups. (3) 'A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison-Kaplansky projection conjecture' (23 September 2026) is about projections, not assembly: it constructs a finitely generated torsion-free Γ_proj = Γ_base * F_N and a projection e in C*_r(Γ_proj) with 0 < τ(e) < 1/2. Its introduction and conclusion add a remark, not a numbered theorem, that the same small trace places [p_0] in K_0(C*_r Γ_base) outside the image of degree-zero coefficient-free reduced assembly for the finitely generated torsion-free Γ_base, citing Baum-Guentner-Willett Prop. 10.3. That is a second, remark-level surjectivity failure in degree zero. (The same manuscript also disproves the Kadison-Kaplansky projection conjecture, which is not a matched problem here.)
entries.delivers: Injectivity fails in degree zero for the coefficient-free reduced assembly map, witnessed by one finitely generated torsion-free group (manuscript 1). Surjectivity fails in degree zero, witnessed by one finitely generated discrete group (manuscript 3, stated as a theorem); manuscript 2 gives the same kind of failure for Γ_base as a remark. Because the bullet asks that the assembly map be an isomorphism in every degree, a failure in degree zero alone refutes it as stated, under the bullet's reading (every discrete group, coefficient C, both injectivity and surjectivity). The manuscripts say so: manuscript 1 says it disproves rational injectivity of the coefficient-free reduced assembly map for torsion-free groups; manuscript 3 says the coefficient-free reduced Baum-Connes conjecture for countable discrete groups is false. Their statement of the conjecture matches the bullet's coefficient-free reading: assembly from equivariant K-homology of the proper classifying space to K_j(C*_r G), for j = 0, 1, with trivial coefficient C. Restrictions: manuscript 1's counterexample is torsion-free and fails only injectivity, in K_0. Manuscript 3's group is not claimed torsion-free; V is an F_p-vector space, so Γ_sur has elements of finite order. The bullet does not require torsion-freeness, so this does not weaken the refutation of the bullet as stated. Manuscript 3's failure is shown in K_0 only.
entries.remains: Nothing is left to refute in the bullet's stated reading: degree zero already refutes it. Not addressed by any of the three manuscripts: (i) degree one, K_1, of the coefficient-free reduced map; (ii) the version with coefficients in a separable G-C*-algebra, which the bullet does not name and which these manuscripts do not treat; (iii) the maximal assembly map, which manuscript 1 says still detects its class (mu^max(h) tensor 1 is nonzero), so it does not refute the maximal version; (iv) the status of the surjectivity failure for Γ_base in manuscript 2, which is a remark-level claim and not a numbered theorem.
entries.direction: disproves the conjecture: injectivity fails in degree zero (manuscript 1); surjectivity fails in degree zero (manuscript 3; remark-level in manuscript 2)
entries.object: No explicit group is written down. In each case the group comes from an existence argument: expanders with large girth, codes over F_p or sampled voltages, Osajda-type labellings, and, in manuscript 1, a finite-witness lemma that extracts a finitely generated subgroup of an infinite construction. The manuscripts say finite presentation is not part of the conclusion. The explicit objects are: in manuscript 1, the degree-zero class h = (Bi)_*[D_{T^2}] in K_0(BΓ), of infinite order and in the kernel of reduced assembly; its vanishing is shown by proof, not by formula. In manuscript 3, the projection b_0 = 1_{0}(T), the spectral projection at zero of an explicit finite-field-module operator T in C*_r(Γ_sur), with trace sum over i of p^(-k_i), where the k_i are chosen with increasing gaps. In manuscript 2, the projection e is given by an explicit compression formula from p_0, but its base group Γ_base is existence-selected.
entries.conditional_on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed in manuscript 1's reduced theorem or manuscript 3's surjectivity theorem, beyond their own constructions and cited published results. Cited results used but not reproved: manuscript 1 uses the twisted spin Dirac index theorem [AS63], in the dimension-two form of [BvE16, Thm. 1], the Emerson-Hudson assembly formula for the torus [EH20, Thm. 1.3], which identifies the assembly image of the torus Dirac class with the rank-zero Bott generator, and the geometric-to-analytic K-homology comparison [BHS07, Thms. 6.1-6.2]. Its maximal-side remark (μ^max(h) tensor 1 nonzero) rests on Hanke-Schick and on a corrected statement of Antonini-Buss-Engel-Siebenand; the reduced claim does not use these. Manuscript 3 uses Lück's trace theorem (Theorem 0.3 of Lück 2002) as a black box for rationality of traces on the assembly image, with the direct-limit domain convention stated in the text; it also uses Osajda's labelling theorem (Theorems 2.7 and 3.2) and Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak expanders. Manuscript 2's surjectivity remark depends on Baum-Guentner-Willett Prop. 10.3 and on Lück's integrality result; its projection theorem does not depend on them.
entries.doubts: (1) Manuscript 1's group is a finitely generated subgroup obtained from an infinite construction by a finite-witness lemma, so the text establishes existence of the group rather than exhibiting it. (2) Manuscript 1's abstract says rational injectivity is disproved for torsion-free groups; its theorem gives one group, which is enough for the universal statement, and the kernel element has infinite order, so the abstract and theorem agree. (3) Manuscript 1's maximal-side discussion records a gap in the all-groups version of the cited Antonini-Buss-Engel-Siebenand result and says it uses the corrected, finitely presented version; the authors say the reduced claim does not depend on it. (4) Manuscript 3's group is not claimed torsion-free, although the abstract's phrase 'for countable discrete groups' suggests a general scope; the theorem gives one group. (5) Manuscript 3's surjectivity conclusion depends on Lück's trace theorem, which is cited, and not on the paper's own analysis. (6) Manuscript 2's surjectivity claim for Γ_base is a remark with a citation, not a proved theorem in its own right. A search of the section files for hedges (sketch, conjecture, assume, erratum, and similar) found no step flagged as sketched in the BC-relevant claims, beyond the items listed here.
